previousCoordinate.reasonReplaced: The legacy point lay approximately 227.1 metres north of the mapped church building and had no source-object contract.

identity.resolvedIdentity: The protected medieval stone church at Prestegårdsbakken 30, identified by OSM way 271994592, Wikidata Q6495600, Kulturminne ID 85456 and Church of Norway building ID 792.
identity.identityProblem: The record combines the church with a wider Oldtidsveien and cultural-landscape narrative. The coordinate must identify the actual church building without treating the gameplay radius as the extent of the churchyard, ancient landscape, pilgrimage route or scattered prehistoric monuments.
identity.splitReason: The church building and immediate church-site environment form one coherent record. The broader Oldtidsveien landscape remains contextual and is represented by other separate place records.

requiredEvidence: heritage and Church of Norway identifiers
official current church identity and address
explicit separation from churchyard, bus stop, parsonage and wider ancient landscape

evidence.finding: The mapped Lutheran church-building polygon has representative point 59.22886, 11.19030 and is linked to Wikidata Q6495600.
evidence.reason: It directly represents the physical church building.

evidence.finding: The entity links OSM way 271994592, Kulturminne ID 85456 and Church of Norway building ID 792, and gives the address Prestegårdsbakken 30.
evidence.reason: Confirms that the mapped building, protected heritage identity and current church register refer to the same church.

evidence.finding: The official church page identifies Skjeberg church at Prestegårdsbakken 30 and describes the church, special grave monuments, parsonage and residence wings as one historical environment.
evidence.reason: Confirms current identity and distinguishes the building from the larger church-site ensemble.

evidence.finding: SNL describes Skjeberg church as a stone church from approximately 1100 with a particularly fine Romanesque soapstone font from the first half of the twelfth century.
evidence.reason: Supports the approximate year and medieval identity.

evidence.finding: Norges Kirker documents the enlarged medieval stone building, its high-site location, churchyard, grave chapels, rune stone, font, altar slab and later building changes.
evidence.reason: Defines the architectural and church-site scope without replacing the direct mapped building geometry.

evidence.finding: The route between Fredrikstad and Skjeberg contains a concentrated collection of prehistoric sites from the Stone, Bronze and Iron Ages.
evidence.reason: Supports the wider landscape framing while not claiming that those sites lie inside the church radius.

evidence.finding: The legacy coordinate lies approximately 227.1 metres north of the mapped church building.
evidence.reason: Replaced because it does not identify the church building.

addressCandidates.rejectionReason: Confirms identity and access, while the building polygon supplies the direct coordinate.

sourceObjectCandidates.rejectionReason: Entity and registry cross-check; the linked OSM building geometry supplies the direct anchor.
The bus stop approximately 170 metres north is access infrastructure, not the church.
The parsonage is a separate historical property in the church-site ensemble.
The wider route and prehistoric landscape do not identify the church building.

rawEvidence.description: Persisted church-building geometry, heritage and registry identity, medieval date, broader landscape context, rejected candidates and radius limits.

decision.nextAction: Applied the Skjeberg medieval church-building point, changed the approximate year from 1180 to the source-supported ca. 1100 and retained the 260-metre gameplay radius. Continue with indreroed_gard_fredrikstad.

notes: The coordinate moves approximately 227.1 metres south.
The marker represents the church building, not the bus stop, cemetery centroid, parsonage, village or Oldtidsveien route.
The year is changed from 1180 to approximately 1100 based on Store norske leksikon.
The broader prehistoric landscape is contextual and not contained by the gameplay radius.
